_status: MEASURED 2026-09-12 on 1da0e33. 2012-06-15 re-measured after the post-blackout re-acquisition work: FusionCore 73.441, robot_localization 18.507 at 99.9 Hz. The two long-blackout sequences were also run twice each overnight on 98134bc, before the outage latch landed, and those medians are recorded below as the reference for their sequences until they are re-run. Every control in every run sat within 0.4% of its baseline, so the data feed was clean throughout.

2012-06-15.note: Long-blackout loss, issue #63: one 461.5 s GNSS gap, 13.9% of the run. Local accuracy is not the problem (RPE@10m 24.8 against RL's 22.6), and the filter tracks to 4.65 m median while fixes are present. The whole loss is drift accumulated blind. Post-blackout re-acquisition now works: 440 m of drift collapses to 13 m within 300 s of fixes returning, against 277 m before. Getting there needed three fixes, and the one that mattered was the outage latch: a single accepted fix landing near the drifted estimate used to disarm recovery for the rest of the run. Repeats on this sequence agree to 2.8%, so a 5% move here is real.

2012-08-20.note: Median of two overnight runs, 122.729 and 117.325, spread 4.6%. RL 10.506 and 10.507 against a 10.52 baseline, so the control is solid. Measured BEFORE the outage latch (1da0e33) and worth re-running: this sequence's adversarial outlier cluster sits at the blackout boundary, which is exactly where that fix changes behaviour. Issue #64.

2013-04-05.note: Median of two overnight runs, 275.951 and 279.303, spread 1.2%, with RL at 268.577 and 267.975 against a 268.639 baseline. No longer void: the control that moved in September has been stable across four runs since. FusionCore still beats RL here. Measured before the outage latch.

_read_this_before_judging_any_regression: The 9x run-to-run spread is NOT universal, which an earlier note here implied. Measured over six unattended runs on 2026-09-12: 2012-06-15 repeats to 2.8%, 2012-08-20 to 4.6%, 2013-04-05 to 1.2%. The historical 32 m to 345 m range was all one sequence, 2013-04-05, and got generalised. So on these sequences a 5 to 10 percent change IS measurable and two runs are enough to see it. Keep the caution for a sequence whose spread has not been measured, and re-check it when adding one. robot_localization remains the control: if it moves more than about a percent between runs, the comparison is void whatever FusionCore did, and that check has already caught one wrong diagnosis (see issue #119).
